commentary_segments.text: The previous rail-to-rail amplifier had the advantage that the supply voltage can be as low as 1.5 V but had at the same time the disadvantage that this supply voltage is hard to predict. In the next rail-to-rail amplifier an internal supply voltage is derived from the external one, which is always set at the minimum possible supply voltage. An exact cross-over situation is always maintained. In this way, a minimum supply voltage is reached which is barely 1.3 V. Moreover, the PSRR is greatly improved as well.
